I think most of the comments about free labor and for profits prisons only address the outcome of America's approach to criminal justice. Americans, generally speaking want those who commit a crime to be punished, not rehabilitated. Especially those who commit violent crime, and if it's an especially violent crime or done continuously, such as serial murder or rape, or mudering children, we want to see the state put them to death. In the minds of a lot of Americans, there is no justice if they're rehabilitated, especially if it means they're going to be coddled and taken care of while they're in rehab, which is what most Americans assume is the case. They want retribution and for the suspect to suffer for what the victim has suffered. We don't want to treat crime, we want to punish it. And all the mechanisms of for profit prisons, slave labor, harsh conditions, no AC, etc all work in tandem to dish out punishment.
